SPECIMEN INFORMATION

 Specimen site  Specimen Type  Block No.  Tumor Percentage
 -  FFPE tissue block  H24-7965  70%

CLINICAL INDICATIONS

Provided diagnosis: Infiltrating glioma

TEST RESULTS AND INTERPRETATION

Positive for MGMT methylation

Detectable methylation in the promoter region of the MGMT gene.

TECHNICAL NOTES

Brief Methodology:

  • FFPE block were used as target material. DNA was extracted from the tissue blocks using FFPE DNA extraction kit, subjected to bi-sulfite treatment using the Epitect bisulfite conversion kit and used as a template for polymerase chain reaction (PCR) using specially designed methylation-specific and non –methylation specific DNA. The resulting product of the PCR was detected using standard procedures. 
  • Detection of product of amplification from methylation-specific probe-set indicates that the cytosine within the DNA was methylated and therefore offered resistance to bi-sulfite treatment and did not convert to uracil. Similarly, signal from non-methylation-specific probes indicate the reverse scenario.

Clinical Background:

  • Epigenetic silencing of the MGMT (O6‐methylguanine–DNA methyl transferase)DNA repair gene by promoter methylation compromises DNA repair mechanism and has been associated with better response to treatment and longer overall survival in glioma patients treated with alkylating agents. 
  • Biology of the process: MGMT is a DNA repair enzyme that reverses alkylation of guanine by transferring the alkyl group to the active site of the enzyme. Diminished MGMT expression due to methylation of CpG sites in the 5’portion of the MGMT gene allows accumulation of alkylguanine DNA which, following incorrect base pairing with thymine, triggers DNA damage signaling and cell death.
  • MGMT methylation is associated with increased sensitivity of glioblastoma to alkylating agents such as BCNU (carmustine), and it also correlates with prolonged progression-free survival in glioma patients treated with temozolamide. 
  • Clinical indications for MGMT promoter methylation testing include high grade glioma (anaplastic astrocytoma or glioblastoma) patient being considered for therapy with an alkylating agent, or glioma patient being considered  for temozolamide therapy.

Limitations:

  • Test results should be interpreted in the context of clinical findings, tumor sampling, and other laboratory data. If results obtained do not match other clinical or laboratory findings, please contact the laboratory for possible interpretation.
